purpose: Teach the published physics-action product to turn a solver-owned basketball/filled-bottle mechanism into a materially credible small film without authoring an outcome pose, project-specific executor or hand-selected event frame.

fixture.mechanism: released regulation-scale basketball + three differently filled active household glass bottles + passive aged court + static area light

requiredReusableChanges: Derive bounded deterministic position, yaw, friction and restitution micro-variation from the graph hash for the realism bottle preset and record every derived initial condition.
Build physically congruent bottle shells with wall thickness, neck/lip/cap/base details and separately visible fill surfaces while retaining the outer visible body as the convex-hull source.
Build a scale-readable procedural court environment with wood-board direction, seams, painted line, baseboard and worn background without external assets.
Frame the cause from narrative actor/target bounds rather than fitting the entire support plane when the scale-cue court preset is active.
Derive a stable group-response window from evaluated target translation and rotation, and allow SETTLED_GROUP_RESPONSE as an effect beat only for a response group.
Keep native blur derived from evaluated projected motion and keep all lights static.
directVisualQuestions: Does the basketball visibly roll, collide, rebound and settle under inertia and support rather than move into an authored pose?
Do at least two bottles respond only after continuous visible contact, with no gap, deep penetration or synchronized pose jump?
Do differing bottle responses and the final arrangement look solver-discovered rather than composed for the camera?
Do basketball scale, seams, pebbling and wear read as a used regulation-scale ball rather than a smooth orange prop?
Do the bottles read as glass containers with wall, shoulder, neck, lip, cap, label and visibly different liquid levels?
Do floor boards, seams, painted line, baseboard, wall and wear cues make the space read at human scale rather than as an empty plane?
Does the cause shot show the ball-to-bottle spatial relationship without shrinking the subjects to fit the whole floor?
Does the contact shot preserve collision direction and native motion blur without hiding the decisive contact?
Does the effect shot come from the measured settled window and show supported resting contacts without posing?
Is the formal result materially and spatially more believable than the accepted RC3 H1 prototype while preserving equally clear physics?
visualVerdictRule: PASS only if all ten questions are YES after direct inspection of all three stills and every frame of the 48-frame contact clip. A photoreal claim remains forbidden even on PASS.
stopRule: Retain and stop on any authored outcome/event frame or post-release pose, project-specific branch, collision/visible-body mismatch, missing continuous contact, fewer than two responders, absent derived settle window, any visual NO, regression, save/reopen mismatch or resource overrun. Correct only reusable semantics in a new version/attempt; never move a final body or type a better frame after observing it.
claimCeiling: A PASS would establish one procedurally art-directed, solver-owned basketball/filled-glass-bottle film lesson and reusable physical-look semantics on this M2 Max. It would not establish liquid dynamics, deformation, breakage, sound, external asset ingestion, cross-platform behavior, production readiness or arbitrary photoreal filmmaking.
